articles.title: How to Build a Prospect Research Pipeline for Cold Email
articles.excerpt: Cold email gets a bad reputation, and honestly, most of it is deserved. The biggest reason? People skip the research step entirely. Sending a well-researched, relevant email to the right person beats…
articles.body: Cold email gets a bad reputation, and honestly, most of it is deserved. The biggest reason? People skip the research step entirely. Sending a well-researched, relevant email to the right person beats blasting hundreds of generic templates every time. In this post, I'll walk through a practical prospect research pipeline that any developer can build or adapt. The Problem with "Spray and Pray" Most cold email workflows look like this: Buy a list of emails Write one template Send to everyone Wonder why the reply rate is near zero The missing step is research . Understanding who you're emailing and why they should care is what separates effective outreach from spam.

articles.title: The Retraction Layer — Or, "We Withdrew the Claim" Is Not the Same as "We Unwound Everything Built on It"
articles.excerpt: A correction edits a sentence. A retraction removes a claim that other things were built on — and the things built on it do not disappear when the sentence does. The pricing page still has the number.…
articles.body: A correction edits a sentence. A retraction removes a claim that other things were built on — and the things built on it do not disappear when the sentence does. The pricing page still has the number. The contract still has the clause. The customer's integration still assumes the endpoint behaves the way the claim said it did. The claim is gone; its children are not. This is the layer under the correction layer, and it is where most audit trails snap. Not because teams refuse to retract, but because they retract the statement and leave the dependents running. The announcement says "we have withdrawn the claim." The world still contains everything the claim caused. A retraction is a reversal, not an edit The correction layer asked: did the people who read the wrong version find out?

articles.title: Stop putting TODO comments in sample code
articles.excerpt: Have you ever copied a code sample from a tutorial, pasted it into your editor, and hit an immediate error? I have, and it is a frustrating experience especially when it's not clear what I need to sup…
articles.body: Have you ever copied a code sample from a tutorial, pasted it into your editor, and hit an immediate error? I have, and it is a frustrating experience especially when it's not clear what I need to supply. It generally looks something like this: # TODO(developer): Uncomment and set your instance # instance_id = "your-instance-id" client = storage . Client ( instance_id ) In technical writing, this is called the copy-paste-completable pattern. When authors write samples, the default instinct is to reach for a TODO(developer) comment to show where user inputs belong. I believe we need to break this habit.

Until Claude Code 2.1.316, that is what a high session got you: a subagent with no effort of its own inherited the session's, unless Claude named a level when it spawned it. The changelog entry for 2.1.316, dated October 31, 2026, reads: "Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's." The official docs stop there.

articles.body: Apache exporter visibility begins at the mod_status boundary An Apache exporter reads a status endpoint and converts the response into Prometheus metrics. Port 9117 is commonly used for the exporter itself. The project can expose request counts, worker state, and server health, but only if Apache's mod_status interface is enabled and reachable from the exporter. The measurements The count-only queries completed on November 5, 2026: Query Matches UTC time port="9117" 4 2026-11-05T00:40:59Z app="apache_exporter" 0 2026-11-05T00:41:00Z http.body="apache_exporter_build_info" 5 2026-11-05T00:41:02Z The application field returned zero. The body and port counts are close but not matched, and neither establishes that an Apache server or exporter is internet-facing.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force launched an experimental Super Strypi rail-launched rocket carrying 13 tiny satellites, but it failed just after liftoff from Hawaii.
articles.body: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms.

articles.title: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix Were Offered the Role of the Joker in The Dark Knight, But Turned it Down

articles.body: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix were both offered the role of Joker in The Dark Knight , but ended up turning it down, according to the film's casting director. When speaking at the Nashville Film Festival (via TV Intelligentsia and Batman News ), Christopher Nolan's longtime casting director John Papsidera revealed that Heath Ledger was not the first choice for Joker in The Dark Knight. He said the script was sent to Leonardo DiCaprio first, who apparently didn't even respond. Then, the offer went to Joaquin Phoenix, who would later win an Oscar for the same role in 2019's Joker . Phoenix told Nolan and Papsidera at the time that he wasn't interested in doing big movies and declined the part. Eventually, they landed on Heath Ledger, and the rest is history.

articles.body: AT&T's smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home. The company says its Connected Life system is the "first" home security product to integrate with Google Home Premium, enabling a bunch of Gemini-powered features that can summarize home events, search your video history, and more.
